events.title: Robert Hooke's Micrographia & Discovery of Biological Cells
events.summary: Published copperplate illustrations of the microscopic world using a compound microscope, coining the biological term 'cell' after observing the honeycomb compartments of cork.
events.impact: Launched cellular microscopy and opened the hidden microscopic universe later expanded by Antonie van Leeuwenhoek's discovery of bacteria.

events.title: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek Discovers Bacteria & Microscopic Life
events.summary: Using handcrafted single-lens glass microscopes magnifying over 250×, Dutch draper Antonie van Leeuwenhoek observed and documented single-celled protozoa and bacteria ('animalcules') in rainwater and infusions.
events.impact: Founded microbiology by revealing the vast unseen microbial biosphere that dominates Earth's ecosystems and human health.

events.title: Edward Jenner Pioneers Vaccination Against Smallpox
events.summary: Demonstrated experimentally that inoculation with mild cowpox (vaccinia) confers protective immunity against deadly smallpox.
events.impact: Founded modern immunology and led directly to the complete global eradication of smallpox in 1980, saving hundreds of millions of lives.

events.title: Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species
events.summary: Presented overwhelming empirical evidence that all species descend with modification from common ancestors driven by natural selection.
events.impact: Unified all of biology under a single explanatory framework and inspired evolutionary algorithms in modern computer science.

events.title: Louis Pasteur Proves Germ Theory & Pioneers Attenuated Vaccines
events.summary: Refuted spontaneous generation with swan-neck flask experiments, demonstrated that airborne microbes cause spoilage and infectious disease, and developed laboratory vaccines against anthrax and rabies.
events.impact: Launched antiseptic surgery, pasteurization, sterile microbiology, and modern infectious-disease medicine—doubling human life expectancy.

events.title: Gregor Mendel's Laws of Discrete Genetic Inheritance
events.summary: Hybridized nearly 28,000 pea plants over eight years to prove heredity operates through discrete paired units ('factors', later called genes) obeying mathematical segregation ratios.
events.impact: Laid the quantitative foundation of classical genetics and the Modern Evolutionary Synthesis.

events.title: Santiago Ramón y Cajal Establishes the Neuron Doctrine
events.summary: Using Camillo Golgi's silver-chromate stain, produced exquisite drawings proving the brain is not a continuous tangled web, but an intricate network of discrete individual cells (neurons) communicating across synaptic gaps.
events.impact: Founded modern cellular neuroscience and directly inspired both connectomics and artificial neural network architectures (1906 Nobel Prize in Medicine).

events.title: Discovery & Development of Penicillin Antibiotics
events.figure: Alexander Fleming, Howard Florey & Ernst Chain
events.summary: Alexander Fleming noticed Penicillium mold lysing Staphylococcus bacteria at St Mary's Hospital, later purified into a life-saving drug by Florey, Chain, and Norman Heatley in Oxford.
events.impact: Ushered in the antibiotic era, transforming once-fatal bacterial infections and enabling modern surgery.

events.title: Discovery of the DNA Double-Helix Structure
events.figure: Rosalind Franklin, Maurice Wilkins, James Watson & Francis Crick
events.summary: Combining Rosalind Franklin and Raymond Gosling's Photo 51 X-ray diffraction pattern at King's College London with structural model-building at Cambridge's Cavendish Lab revealed DNA's complementary double helix.
events.impact: Immediately explained the physical copying mechanism of heredity and launched the entire field of molecular biology.

events.title: Frederick Sanger Invents Chain-Termination DNA Sequencing
events.summary: Developed dideoxy chain-termination chemistry at MRC LMB to read exact nucleotide base sequences (A, C, G, T), earning Sanger his second Nobel Prize in Chemistry (1980).
events.impact: Provided the core reading engine of modern genomics and directly powered the first sequencing of the human genome.

events.title: Invention of Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR)
events.summary: Conceived thermal-cycling exponential DNA amplification using heat-stable Taq polymerase, turning a single trace DNA molecule into billions of copies in hours.
events.impact: Indispensable cornerstone of medical diagnostics, ancient DNA paleogenomics, forensics, and genetic engineering.

events.title: Completion of the Human Genome Project
events.summary: An international public consortium across 20 centers in six countries mapped and released ~3 billion base pairs of human euchromatic DNA freely online under the Bermuda Principles.
events.impact: Catalyzed genomic medicine, plummeting sequencing costs by more than a million-fold and launching precision oncology and population genomics.

events.title: Shinya Yamanaka Discovers Induced Pluripotent Stem (iPS) Cells
events.summary: Demonstrated that introducing just four transcription factors (Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, c-Myc) reprograms mature adult skin cells back into embryonic-like pluripotent stem cells.
events.impact: Revolutionized regenerative medicine, personalized disease modeling, and 3D human organoids (2012 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine).

events.title: CRISPR-Cas9 Programmable RNA-Guided Genome Editing
events.figure: Jennifer Doudna, Emmanuelle Charpentier, Martin Jinek & Krzysztof Chylinski
events.summary: Repurposed a bacterial immune defense into a programmable molecular scissor using a single guide RNA (sgRNA) to cut any chosen DNA sequence with pinpoint precision.
events.impact: Democratized gene editing worldwide, won the 2020 Chemistry Nobel, and led to the first FDA/MHRA-approved CRISPR sickle-cell therapy (2023).

events.title: Nucleoside-Modified mRNA Vaccines Validated Globally
events.figure: Katalin Karikó, Drew Weissman & Global mRNA Teams
events.summary: Decades of foundational RNA modification work (pseudouridine substitution preventing destructive inflammation, paired with lipid nanoparticles) enabled safe, >90%-effective COVID-19 vaccines designed within days of viral sequencing.
events.impact: Saved millions of lives, earned the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, and opened a programmable platform for personalized cancer vaccines.

events.title: AlphaFold 3, De Novo Protein Design & the AI Science Nobels
events.figure: Demis Hassabis, John Jumper, David Baker, Geoffrey Hinton & John Hopfield
events.summary: AlphaFold 3 extended atomic diffusion prediction to proteins, DNA, RNA, and small-molecule drugs, while both the 2024 Physics and Chemistry Nobel Prizes recognized foundational neural networks and AI protein science.
events.impact: Cemented artificial intelligence as a core foundational instrument of physics, chemistry, and molecular biology.

trails.title: From X-Ray Diffraction to AI-Designed Medicines
trails.tagline: Follow a 70-year chain connecting Cavendish crystal physics, Nobel molecular biology, open databases, and AlphaFold.

stops.title: University of Cambridge (Cavendish Lab)
stops.bridge: Lawrence Bragg's X-ray crystallography physics at the Cavendish spawned a dedicated unit to decode the 3D atomic shapes of hemoglobin and DNA.

stops.title: MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology
stops.bridge: Decades of X-ray crystallography and cryo-EM breakthroughs at MRC LMB—earning 12 Nobel Prizes—populated the world's experimental protein archives.

stops.title: EMBL-EBI Bioinformatics Hub
stops.bridge: Curated global protein sequences and experimental PDB structures into clean open datasets—giving Google DeepMind the ground truth to crack protein folding.

stops.title: Google DeepMind
stops.bridge: AlphaFold 2 solved the 50-year protein folding grand challenge (2024 Chemistry Nobel), motivating a dedicated sister company to turn predictions into drugs.

stops.title: Isomorphic Labs
stops.bridge: Co-built AlphaFold 3 to model drug-protein-DNA complexes in silico, converging with high-throughput genomic medicine and CRISPR labs.

stops.title: Broad Institute of MIT & Harvard
stops.bridge: Unites AI molecular models with single-cell human genetics and base/prime CRISPR editing to bring programmable medicines to patients.

trails.title: From Living Brain Circuits to Agile Humanoid Machines
trails.tagline: Trace the feedback loop from silicon neural probes and biological connectomes to Vision-Language-Action robots.

stops.title: HHMI Janelia Research Campus
stops.bridge: Mapped the complete fruit-fly brain connectome and co-engineered Neuropixels silicon probes (with imec) to record thousands of living neurons at once.

stops.title: Allen Institute for Brain Science
stops.bridge: Scaled open brain mapping to 5,300+ mammalian cell types and cortical connectomes, fueling computational theories of biological learning.

stops.title: Vector Institute (Toronto)
stops.bridge: Geoffrey Hinton turned brain-inspired artificial neural networks and backpropagation into AlexNet (2012), igniting modern deep learning.

stops.title: UC Berkeley BAIR
stops.bridge: Extended deep neural networks from pixels to physical action via deep reinforcement learning and open cross-embodiment robot manipulation datasets.

stops.title: Physical Intelligence (π)
stops.bridge: Co-founded by Berkeley and Stanford roboticists to train generalist Vision-Language-Action policies capable of folding laundry and manipulating tools.

stops.title: Boston Dynamics
stops.bridge: Pairs emerging AI dexterity with decades of dynamic whole-body hardware mastery culminating in the all-electric Atlas humanoid.

stops.title: ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab
stops.bridge: Demonstrates how massively parallel GPU reinforcement learning trains rugged legged robots in minutes to hike Alpine mountains and lunar craters.

trails.title: Decoding Life: From Heredity to Genomic AI
trails.tagline: Follow DNA from its discovery as genetic code through million-fold sequencing drops, CRISPR, and 40B-parameter genome models.

stops.title: The Rockefeller University
stops.bridge: In 1944, Avery, MacLeod, and McCarty proved here that DNA—not protein—is the molecule carrying genetic heredity.

stops.title: Wellcome Sanger Institute
stops.bridge: Using Frederick Sanger's chain-termination sequencing, decoded one-third of the Human Genome Project and established open global genomic data.

stops.title: Cambridge Dept. of Chemistry
stops.bridge: Just up the road, Balasubramanian and Klenerman invented Solexa/Illumina sequencing-by-synthesis—slashing whole-genome costs from $100M to under $200.

stops.title: Innovative Genomics Institute (CRISPR)
stops.bridge: Once biology could read genomes cheaply, Jennifer Doudna's CRISPR-Cas9 gave humanity the molecular word processor to edit DNA precisely.

stops.title: Arc Institute (Palo Alto)
stops.bridge: Now trains 40B-parameter genomic foundation models (Evo 2) across 9.3 trillion DNA bases to design novel genetic circuits and Virtual Cells.

stops.title: AHRI & KRISP (Durban)
stops.bridge: Brings high-speed genomics to global public health—tracking emerging viral variants in real time across Africa to protect the entire world.

trails.title: Mapping the Living Brain
trails.tagline: Journey from foundational synaptic biology and the first worm connectome to silicon Neuropixels probes and brain-spine interfaces.

stops.title: Institut Pasteur (Paris)
stops.bridge: Jean-Pierre Changeux isolated the first neurotransmitter receptor (nicotinic acetylcholine receptor) here, revealing the molecular switches of synaptic communication.

stops.title: MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology
stops.bridge: Sydney Brenner and John White mapped the first complete nervous system in history—every neuron and synapse of the nematode C. elegans—proving whole-brain connectomics was possible.

stops.title: imec Leuven (Neuropixels Silicon)
stops.bridge: Repurposed CMOS semiconductor lithography to fabricate hair-thin Neuropixels probes packed with hundreds of electrodes recording thousands of live neurons simultaneously.

stops.title: HHMI Janelia Research Campus
stops.bridge: Co-engineered Neuropixels and GCaMP optical neural sensors while reconstructing dense electron-microscopy synaptic wiring diagrams of the fruit-fly brain.

stops.title: Allen Institute for Brain Science
stops.bridge: Scaled open brain mapping to 5,300+ mammalian cell types and cubic-millimeter cortical connectomes (MICrONS), turning neural architecture into open public data.

stops.title: EPFL AI & Neuro-X Ecosystem
